diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.empty: No problems found - everything looks fine.
diagfinding.pool_branch_missing.title: Pool “{pool}” has an unreachable branch: {path}
diagfinding.pool_branch_missing.body: {path} does not exist or is not a directory. This disk may have been removed from the machine, or is not mounted. While this stands, the pool runs without this branch - the folders on it disappear from the pool's view, even though nothing was actually deleted.
diagfinding.pool_not_mounted.title: Pool “{pool}” is not mounted
diagfinding.pool_not_mounted.body: The pool is configured but not currently reachable at {mountpoint}. Every bind mount and share behind it is unreachable while this is the case.
diagfinding.pool_cache_files_off.title: Pool “{pool}” runs without a page cache (cache.files=off)
diagfinding.mergerfs_outdated.title: The installed mergerfs ({installed}) is older than the kernel could use
diagfinding.mergerfs_outdated.body: The running kernel ({kernel}) supports FUSE IO passthrough, but the installed mergerfs does not - that needs {needed} or newer. Under passthrough the kernel reads and writes the branch file directly, skipping the mergerfs process entirely, which gives near native speed; without it every read and write makes the round trip through mergerfs. It shows up most on programs that write in small pieces, such as a torrent client. Distribution packages are typically years behind; mergerfs's own documentation recommends installing from the releases page rather than via apt. After upgrading, Diagnostics will offer to turn it on with one click.
diagfinding.pool_needs_remount.title: Pool “{pool}” is not running what is configured
diagfinding.pool_needs_remount.body: The running mergerfs differs from the saved settings in: {options}. Some options (write aggregation, passthrough) can only be adopted when the filesystem is mounted, so saving alone is not enough - until then the pool keeps running the old settings, and any measurement measures the old state. The fix remounts the pool and brings the bind mounts on top of it back up afterwards (they are stopped along with the pool).
diagfinding.pool_needs_remount.confirm: Pool “{pool}” will be remounted and the bind mounts on top of it brought back up. Shares will be unreachable for a few seconds. Continue?
diagfinding.pool_passthrough_available.b: Both the kernel and the installed mergerfs support FUSE IO passthrough, but it is not enabled on this pool. With it on, the kernel reads and writes the branch file directly, skipping the mergerfs process - the largest available win for small, scattered writes. It has a cost: moveonenospc does not work under it (mergerfs never sees the writes, so it cannot see a branch fill up), and write aggregation cannot be used alongside it. The fix enables passthrough, turns off what it conflicts with, and remounts the pool.
diagfinding.pool_passthrough_available.c: IO passthrough (rw) will be enabled on pool “{pool}”. This turns off moveonenospc and write aggregation, and remounts the pool. Continue?
diagfinding.pool_cache_files_off.body: In this mode mergerfs works in direct_io: no kernel page cache, and no shared mmap support either. That has two visible consequences. Programs that use mmap (qBittorrent/libtorrent 2.x, sqlite-based applications) fail outright or fall back to a slower mode. And programs that write in small pieces pay a separate round trip into the mergerfs process for every single write, which can drop write throughput to a fraction of what the disk can do. Unless you chose this specifically to keep RAM use down, set the file page cache to “auto-full” in the pool editor.
diagfinding.bind_source_missing.title: Bind mount “{bind}”'s source does not exist: {path}
diagfinding.bind_source_missing.body: The directory {path} is missing. It is created the same way as recreating a missing source from the editor: as a new ZFS dataset when the parent is one, otherwise as a plain directory, then given the standard share permissions (nobody:nogroup, 0777).
diagfinding.bind_source_missing.confirm: The missing source directory will be created (owned nobody:nogroup, mode 0777). Continue?
diagfinding.bind_source_wrong_perms.titl: Bind mount “{bind}”'s source has the wrong ownership
diagfinding.bind_source_wrong_perms.body: {path} is not owned nobody:nogroup with mode 0777. With Samba's “force user = nobody”, that means clients can list the folder but cannot write into it - exactly what happened the last time a missing bind source was recreated.
diagfinding.bind_source_wrong_perms.conf: The source's owner will be set to nobody:nogroup and its mode to 0777. Continue?
diagfinding.bind_not_mounted.title: Bind mount “{bind}” is not mounted
diagfinding.bind_not_mounted.body: The source exists, but the bind mount is not currently mounted at {target}, so users would see an empty folder there.
diagfinding.bind_not_mounted.confirm: This bind mount will be mounted. Continue?
diagfinding.bind_source_single_branch.ti: “{bind}” currently exists on only one disk of pool “{pool}”
diagfinding.bind_source_single_branch.bo: It lives on branch {branch} and nowhere else in the pool - mergerfs only places a newly created folder on one branch. Removing that disk from the pool right now would make this folder - and everything the bind mount shows through it - disappear from the union view, even though nothing would actually be deleted.
diagfinding.share_path_missing.title: Share “{share}”'s path does not exist: {path}
diagfinding.share_path_missing.body: {path} does not exist or is not a directory. Check that the backing pool/disk is mounted before recreating the folder - blindly creating the missing path on the root filesystem would hide the real mount failure underneath it.
diagfinding.share_wrong_perms.title: Share “{share}” has the wrong ownership
diagfinding.share_wrong_perms.body: {path} is not owned nobody:nogroup with mode 0777. With Samba's “force user = nobody”, that means clients can list the folder but cannot write into it.
diagfinding.share_wrong_perms.confirm: The share's owner will be set to nobody:nogroup and its mode to 0777. Continue?
diagfinding.share_tree_cache.title: Share “{share}” has a client-side tree cache in its root: {files}
diagfinding.share_tree_cache.body: Total Commander's directory tree cache ({files}) is sitting in the root of {path}. TC navigates from that copy instead of asking the server, so once it goes stale, opening folders created since then fails with no error dialog at all - the user just gets a beep. Nothing looks wrong on the server meanwhile: permissions, ACLs, the Samba config and even smbclient run from the host all come back clean, because nothing is wrong there. And because the file lives on the share, it is shared state: every client browsing with TC works from the same stale copy. The fix deletes it, and TC recreates it on its next run. To stop it coming back, point the client's tree files at a local folder with the TreeFileLocation key in the [Configuration] section of wincmd.ini.
diagfinding.share_tree_cache.confirm: These will be deleted from the share root: {files}. The client recreates them if it needs them. Continue?
diagfinding.share_client_clutter.title: Share “{share}” has client-side clutter in its root: {files}
diagfinding.share_client_clutter.body: Cache files left behind by Finder or Explorer ({files}) are sitting in the root of {path}. They break nothing, but they belong on the client rather than on shared storage: every user sees them, and they end up in backups. The fix deletes them, and the client recreates them if it needs them.
diagfinding.share_client_clutter.confirm: These will be deleted from the share root: {files}. The client recreates them if it needs them. Continue?
diagfinding.share_unknown_user.title: Share “{share}” references a user that no longer exists: {user}
diagfinding.share_unknown_user.body: “{user}” appears in the share's access list but is no longer among the users. Edit the share to remove or replace the reference.
diagfinding.share_unknown_group.title: Share “{share}” references a group that no longer exists: {group}
diagfinding.share_unknown_group.body: “{group}” appears in the share's access list but is no longer among the groups. Edit the share to remove or replace the reference.
diagfinding.disk_mount_uuid_missing.titl: Disk mount “{name}”'s UUID cannot be found: {uuid}
diagfinding.disk_mount_uuid_missing.body: No block device currently carries this UUID - the disk may have been removed, replaced, or reformatted. Check the disk before changing anything in the configuration.
diagfinding.disk_mount_not_mounted.title: Disk mount “{name}” is not mounted
diagfinding.disk_mount_not_mounted.body: The disk is configured but not currently reachable at {mountpoint}.
diagfinding.disk_mount_not_mounted.confi: This disk will be mounted. Continue?
diagfinding.pool_unit_missing.title: Pool “{pool}”'s systemd unit is missing
diagfinding.pool_unit_missing.body: The pool is configured in the app, but its systemd unit file is not on disk, so it will not mount automatically on the next boot.
diagfinding.pool_unit_missing.confirm: The systemd unit will be rewritten, and the pool mounted if it isn't already. Continue?
diagfinding.pool_unit_drift.title: Pool “{pool}”'s systemd unit does not match its current settings
diagfinding.pool_unit_drift.body: The unit file on disk does not match what the pool's current settings would generate - someone may have hand-edited it, or an earlier save was never applied. While this stands, the next restart mounts the pool with the old settings.
diagfinding.pool_unit_drift.confirm: The systemd unit will be rewritten to match the current settings. Continue?
diagfinding.bind_unit_missing.title: Bind mount “{bind}”'s systemd unit is missing
diagfinding.bind_unit_missing.body: The bind mount is configured in the app, but its systemd unit file is not on disk, so it will not mount automatically on the next boot.
diagfinding.bind_unit_missing.confirm: The systemd unit will be rewritten, and the bind mount mounted if it isn't already. Continue?
diagfinding.wsdd2_publishes_ipv6.title: wsdd2 is publishing this host's link-local IPv6 address ({interfaces})
diagfinding.wsdd2_publishes_ipv6.body: wsdd2 answers LLMNR name queries as well as WS-Discovery, and without “-4” it replies with every address on the interface - including the link-local IPv6 on {interfaces}. Windows prefers that AAAA answer, cannot route an fe80:: address without a zone id, and only falls back to IPv4 once the TCP connect times out. Expect intermittent 0x80070035 (“the network path was not found”) when opening \\<host>, and multi-second stalls at startup in any application that touches a mapped drive. The fix installs a systemd drop-in restricting wsdd2 to IPv4; discovery keeps working.
diagfinding.wsdd2_publishes_ipv6.confirm: wsdd2 will be restricted to IPv4 and restarted. If this build does not know the option, the change is undone and the packaged unit restored. Continue?
diagfinding.discovery_unit_inactive.body: The shares stay reachable by typing \\<host>\<share>, but this host will not appear when browsing the network. nmbd serves NetBIOS name lookups and the browse list for older clients, wsdd2 the WS-Discovery that Windows 10 and 11 use since SMB1 was removed - both are wanted, neither replaces the other.
diagfinding.discovery_unit_inactive.conf: {unit} will be enabled and started. Continue?
